source.title: Superior resilience to poisoning and amenability to unlearning in quantum machine learning

record.tranche_reason: Tests how classical and quantum classifiers generalize under training-label corruption, extending generalization findings to quantum models and a poisoning setting. It does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports label-flipping results on natural labels, but does not test fitting random labels or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example claims. Feature randomization is out-of-distribution noise, and unlearning results do not measure the claim’s generalization behavior; neither is included as a row.
record.test_reason: The study measures robustness to training-data corruption and unlearning, rather than any listed version. It cites memorization capacity but does not establish near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization. Its capacity sweep does not identify interpolation or train to convergence, and its Hessian-trace ratio does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the label-flipping conclusion but omits the second central conclusion: approximate unlearning methods recover QNN validation performance more effectively than for the MLP and can outperform QNN retraining within the limited unlearning window. The authors attribute both advantages to landscape stability; this is their mechanistic interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: Compares an MLP and parameterized quantum circuits on binary MNIST and XXZ tasks under label flipping; it does not reproduce the original claim’s random-label memorization experiments. Initial training uses Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (MNIST versus XXZ); label-noise ratio α; model class and capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: On binary MNIST and XXZ tasks, MLP validation accuracy declines with label flipping, whereas QNN validation accuracy remains high below approximately 50% corruption and collapses above it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested QNNs preserve clean held-out accuracy under moderate label flipping better than the tested MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, the noisy-to-clean Hessian-trace ratio is O(10^2) for the MLP and approximately one or smaller for the QNN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested QNN's local loss curvature changes less under label corruption than the tested MLP's.

record.problems: The paper reports qualitative trends and figure descriptions rather than exact accuracy values in the supplied text. Experiments use binary tasks and five optimization runs; the authors note that broader architectures, datasets, tasks, and unlearning methods remain for future study.
record.rows_left_out: Feature-randomization results concern out-of-distribution noise, and unlearning results concern repair procedures rather than the claim’s natural-label generalization behavior. They were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting, chance held-out performance with random labels, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.

Test-error behavior when widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold under training to convergence. Supplement II varies capacity under label corruption without establishing these conditions.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across regularization and data regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing high-memorization examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the reported corruption effects. The supplied source does not establish the record's Nature Communications publication status.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit random labels or compare held-out accuracy under random versus natural labels.
Does not sweep width beyond interpolation on natural labels.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for held-out performance.
Does not compare batch sizes or large-batch generalization gaps.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and compare with random removals.
